title: kwft7a
Illegal power that Mu'awiya has usurped
hook: In Mu'awiya's years the caliphate turned into kingship; Imam Ali was cursed and Yazid became crown prince.
scenes.0.text: The Prophet had predicted that the caliphate would last thirty years after him, then turn into a biting kingdom. With the reconciliation of Hasan, it's been 30 years. One day the governor said, "I am the first of the kings". The caliphate was entrusted to run the affairs of the nation according to the will of Allah. The mu'awiyah made the trust his family's property. The palace in Damascus grew bigger every year. The common wealth of the nation flowed into the sack of a family. The people of the House were denied the right to live there, and were cursed on the scaffolding.
scenes.1.text: Mu'awiya, governor of Damascus during the Ottoman Caliphate, built **Hadra** in Damascus, which means Green Palace. The splendor of the palace was visible from afar. Abu Zar al-Gifari, one of the Prophet's closest companions, stood in front of Mu'awiya one day and said to him, "If you have built this palace with Allah's money, it is treason, if you have built it with your own money, it is excess". This is reported in the work of Belazuri called Ensâb'l-Eshrâf. Mu'awiya was unable to reply, but complained to the Caliph Uthman of Medina about Abu Zer. Abu Zer was banished from Damascus and eventually died alone in the Rebeza desert. Abu Zer was a beloved companion of the Prophet who was not afraid to speak the truth in front of the palace.
scenes.2.text: Mu'awiya adopted a man named **Ziyad** as his brother, declaring him the son of his father Abu Sufyan. It's called heating, or adding soy. The Prophet said, "The child belongs to the owner of the bed". According to this ruling, a child is considered the offspring of his mother's husband and it is forbidden to add him to another's offspring on the charge of adultery. Ziyad was born in the bed of Ubayd, the husband of a maid called Sumayya, and for years Ziyad b. He was known as **Ubeyd**. He knew that it was forbidden, so he violated the Prophet's clear command to strengthen his power. Ziad, who was declared a brother, was made governor of Kufa and Basra. In these cities, he marched ruthlessly on those who loved **Ali**. A false genealogy had become a whip used to crush the friends of the Ehl-i-Beit.
scenes.3.text: On the orders of Mu'awiya, the curse of **Ali** was recited from the pulpits in the Friday sermons. The most blessed day of the week turned into a day of insult to the Prophet's brother and son-in-law. The Mu'awiya asked Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas why he did not curse Ali. He wrote letters to his governors, ordering them to insult Ali and punish those who loved him. This persecution lasted until years later, when the Umayyad Caliph Umar bin Abdulaziz banned it. In those years, loving the Ahl al-Bayt was considered a crime in the land of the Umayyads.
scenes.4.text: **Hucr b. Adi** was one of Ali's valiant companions and commanders in Kufa. He refused to accept the curse read from the pulpit and openly opposed it. **Ziyad**, the governor of Kufa, arrested him and sent him to Damascus with about twelve of his companions. In the 51st year of the Hijrah, they were massacred at Merju Azra near Damascus. The advocate defended this blood against those who challenged him. The head of **Amr b. Hamk**, one of Ali's friends, was cut off and carried from city to city. The curse on the pulpit, so it turned to blood.
scenes.5.text: In the last years of his life, Mu'awiya forcibly proclaimed his son Yazid as successor. The heir is the person who takes over the throne after the death of the ruler. So the caliphate became a dynasty passed down from father to son. Mu'awiya also broke his promise to Hasan: "I will not appoint a caliph after me". In Medina, Husayn did not submit to this succession. Abdullah b. Umar, Abdullah and B. Zubair and Abdurrahman b. And Abi Bekir did not agree.
scenes.6.text: Yazid was known for drinking wine, playing with hounds and monkeys, and publicly confessing his sins. These accusations made against him by the people of Medina are recorded in the history books. To bequeath to such a man was to justify his actions. His Holiness Husayn refused to give this pledge. A pledge of allegiance. The Prophet's grandson would not pledge allegiance to anyone who openly violated his grandfather's religion. Husayn would say to the governor of Medina, "No one like me would betray someone like him". Karbala was a bitter consequence of Mu'awiya's decision to take over.
scenes.7.text: In the year 60 of the Hijrah, Mu'awiya died in the month of Recep and the throne passed to Yazid. As soon as Yazid took the throne, he sent an order to the governor of Medina: The governor summoned Husayn and announced this order. Husayn did not give in and soon left Medina for Mecca with his family. He did not surrender his grandfather's religion to the rule of a wine-drinking ruler. The end of this road was to be the testimony at Karbala. The order of the kingdom was established by the father. And the son would cut off the Euphrates to the Prophet's grandson.
sunni.0.says: The hadith «The caliphate is thirty years, then it will be kingship».
sunni.1.says: Another report of the same hadith.
sunni.2.says: Mu'awiya asking Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas why he did not curse Imam Ali.
sunni.3.says: Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Bakr's objection to the allegiance to Yazid.
sunni.4.says: Ibn Abbas's saying about Mu'awiya, «he is a jurist».
sunni.5.says: The events of 51 AH, Ziyad being declared Mu'awiya's brother, and Yazid's succession.
shia.0.says: Mu'awiya ordering his governors to have Imam Ali cursed; relayed from al-Mada'ini.
shia.1.says: Mu'awiya's power, Hujr b. Adi, and Yazid's succession.
shia.2.says: Mu'awiya has al-Khadra built in Damascus. Abu Dharr says, if it is from God's wealth, it is treachery, if from his own wealth, it is waste. Mu'awiya falls silent.
disputes.0.title: 1jy4ts
Did the caliphate turn into kingship?
disputes.0.sunni: It is agreed that Mu'awiya took over the government after 41 AH. In the Sunni reading he is a caliph; his rule is counted as an ijtihad and as peace.
disputes.0.shia: It is agreed that Mu'awiya took over the government after 41 AH. In the Shia account the succession, the istilhaq and the cursing show that the caliphate turned into inheritance and force.
disputes.1.title: 1ul0hv9
Responsibility for the killing of Hujr
disputes.1.sunni: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is told in the sources. Who held the order is debated; many Sunni scholars regard this killing as a mistake.
disputes.1.shia: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is told in the sources. In the Shia account this is a punishment given for his refusal to curse Imam Ali.
questions.0: The Prophet had announced that the caliphate would last for thirty years, and with the peace of Hasan, these thirty years were completed. Why do you think Mu'awiya's announcement of his son's accession to the throne comes with this news?
questions.1: Mu'awiya cursed Ali in his Friday sermons and Hucr b. When she refused the Adî curse, she was killed at Mercü Azra. Why do you think the Mu'awiya curse binds those who reject it to death?
questions.2: Do you think that Husayn and Abdurrahman b. Why didn't Abi Bekir agree to Yazid's succession?
summary: After 41 AH Mu'awiya established a Damascus-centered rule. He declared Ziyad his brother. Imam Ali was cursed in the sermons. Hujr b. Adi was killed and his son Yazid became crown prince. In Sunni books Mu'awiya is also remembered as a Companion and a ruler. In the Shia account these years prepared the road to Karbala.
key: From caliphate to kingdom: Hujr, Ziyad and Yazid's succession
notes.0: Abu Dharr said to Mu'awiya about the Khadra Palace, 'if it is God's wealth, it is treachery, if it is your own wealth, it is waste.' He was expelled from Syria and died alone at Rabadha.
notes.1: The hadith «caliphate thirty years, then kingship» appears in Tirmidhi 2226 and Abu Dawud 4646.
notes.2: Mu'awiya declared Ziyad b. Abihi his brother (istilhaq, 44 AH).
notes.3: Cursing Imam Ali from the pulpits became an established practice.
notes.4: Hujr b. Adi was killed at Marj Adhra in 51 AH because he refused the cursing.
notes.5: He declared his son Yazid crown prince; Mu'awiya died in 60 AH and the process leading to Karbala began.
sunni.6.says: Abu Zer's saying to Mu'awiya for the Hadra palace: "If you have done it from Allah's wealth, treachery, if you have done it from your own wealth, it is excess".
